parts.label: a
parts.text:
Write down the database schema of all tables. Identify all primary keys and foreign keys, if any.
(2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Describe the relationship represented by the ER diagram.  (2 marks)
[--Answer:

Primary key: TID                     Foreign key: N/A
Member (MID, MNAME, TID)

--]

items.stem:
A coffee brand that sources and sells different types of speciality coffee from around the world. They maintain a database table COFFEE to store information about the coffee they offer and the farm where it is produced.
COFFEE
Field name
Description
CID
Identity code of each coffee bean
CNAME
Name of the coffee bean
FID
Identity code of the farm where the coffee is produced
FARM
The name of the farm where the coffee is produced
FRID
Identity code of the farmer
FARMER
The name of the farmer
Primary key: CID

parts.label: a
parts.text: A new coffee farm is collaborating with the brand, but they haven’t provided the coffee beans. However, the brand wishes to insert the data of the farm and farmers into the COFFEE table first. Explain why an insertion anomaly occurs. (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text: What is the normalisation form of this table? Explain briefly.  (2 marks)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Refer to the answer in (b), and normalise the table to the next normalisation form. Write the database schema for the tables, underline the primary key and identify the foreign key.  (5 marks)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The requirements of the database are described below:
Each type of coffee bean has to be produced by exactly one farm. A farm can produce more than a kind of coffee bean. A farmer works in exactly one farm, and a farm includes many farmers.
Complete the ER diagram for the database design below. It is not necessary to draw attributes.
(3 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) Since the farm has not provided the coffee beans to the brand yet, the CID can only be NULL. While CID is the primary key of the COFFEE table and a primary key cannot be NULL, the record cannot be inserted.
(b) Second normal form (2NF). The table has no multi-value fields, repeating groups, or partial dependency. Yet, FARM depends on FID rather than depending directly on the primary key CID, which violates 3NF because of transitive functional dependency.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
COFFEE (CID, CNAME, FID)
Foreign key: FID
FARM(FID, FARM_NAME)
FARMER(FRID, FARMER_NAME, FID)
Foreign key: FID
